chunks: Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar from Safwan ibn Yahya from Mansur ibn Hazim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (Imam al-Sadiq), the source of the narration
key_terms.أَبُو عَلِيٍّ الْأَشْعَرِيُّ: Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, a narrator in the chain
key_terms.صَفْوَانُ بْنُ يَحْيَى: Safwan ibn Yahya, a narrator in the chain
key_terms.مَنْصُورُ بْنُ حَازِمٍ: Mansur ibn Hazim, a narrator in the chain
key_terms.مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ الْجَبَّارِ: Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, a narrator in the chain
key_terms.مِثْلُهُ: Like it / The same as it, indicating repetition of a previous ruling

ai.seo_question: What does the phrase 'mithluhu' indicate in Shia hadith literature?
ai.summary: This is a concise hadith from the book Tahdhib al-Ahkam, indicating that the ruling or narration previously mentioned is repeated or identical to the current one. It serves as a reference to a preceding legal ruling regarding bequests. In the context of Chapter 11, which discusses the permissibility of bequeathing one-third or less of one's estate, this 'mithluhu' (like it) format confirms the consistency of Imam al-Sadiq’s (AS) position on the limits of voluntary bequests (wasiyyah) distinct from the obligatory shares of heirs.
